slides.texte_overlay: 1. Playing a musical instrument. Piano, guitar, drums. Reading music, coordinating both hands and keeping rhythm trains memory, focus and patience at the same time.
2. Building with your hands. Woodworking, models, repairing old bikes. Solving physical problems teaches planning and spatial thinking that screens never will.
3. Learning to code. Small projects, simple games, a personal website. Coding trains logic and breaks big problems into small, clear steps.
4. Debating with friends. Pick a topic over dinner and argue the side you disagree with. It sharpens your reasoning and makes you a far better listener.
Bonus: a daily dose of curiosity. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it feeds every other hobby with new ideas.
slides.texte_sophia: Bonus: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It feeds every other hobby with new ideas.

slides.texte_overlay: Why it works: intelligence grows when you do hard things regularly. Hobbies that challenge you a little every week build a sharper mind than any quick trick.
Pick one and stick with it for three months. Not four at once. Depth beats variety, and the progress you feel after a few months will keep you going.
